transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-01
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Priya Ramaswamy (DevBridge CTO), Alex Monroe (DevBridge Lead Eng), Casey Liu (DevOps)
---
Auto sections (may be imperfect):
Summary: Walkthrough of SDK onramp and auth setup; emphasis on KMS flow and sandbox provisioning. Customer asks about Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and PCI/data residency concerns.
Topics: SDK quickstart, API keys vs service accounts, KMS integrations, sandbox CI secrets, Dedicated capacity and SLAs, Optimize knobs (batching, KV cache).
Action items: Jordan to send pricing and security pack; Samira to provision sandbox with demo keys; Alex to provide load profile.
Questions: How do we rotate keys with their KMS? What is the expected latency for small-chat workloads?
---
Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE for the account, with Samira on the technical side. we can run through python/typescript quickstarts, auth, and then KMS and sandbox stuff.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks. we have a tight timeline, looking to decide on a proof of concept by mid-May. main asks are security (SOC2), ability to integrate our KMS, and predictable latency.
[00:30] Samira: totally. we'll aim to show both the SDK flow and the recommended auth patterns. quick question, alex, are you planning to run this as hosted first or do you already prefer Dedicated?
[00:42] Alex: leaning Dedicated — predictable throughput and we can isolate traffic — but cost is a concern. we need to understand the trade when you enable KV cache and batching.
[00:55] Jordan: good callout. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and clearer SLOs, hosted is faster to get started. we can do a hybrid — start hosted to validate, then flip to Dedicated for pilot.
[01:10] Casey: on the KMS front, we use HashiCorp vault in prod and GCP KMS in staging. rotation every 30 days. we need to prove key rotation in the flow.
[01:23] Samira: we support service account key wrapping with customer-managed keys (CMK) — redwood private has a KMS handshake where keys never leave your control. i'll show the demo wiring in the sandbox. note: sometimes the transcript says K-V cash, sorry.
[01:40] Priya: that's helpful. also need to see the integration with our CI so secrets don't leak into logs.
[01:48] Samira: recommended pattern is short-lived tokens issued via a service account and an internal token exchange in your CI; avoid long-lived API keys in pipelines. we'll include a sample terraform / github actions snippet.
[02:05] Jordan: ok let's jump into the SDK quickstart. Samira, can you share your screen?
[02:14] Samira: yeah, pulling up the python quickstart. index file, pip install redwood-sdk (note: package name in demo may change as product evolves). basic usage: set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var or use REDWOOD_SA_TOKEN for service account flow.
[02:35] Alex: show the typescript bits too — we have a node service that will call endpoints.
[02:40] Samira: absolutely. typescript import is similar, npm i @redwood/inference (pseudo name in demo). example: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); client.generate(...). streaming is supported via event handlers.
[02:59] Priya: do you recommend streaming or full responses for low-latency chat UX?
[03:05] Samira: streaming reduces time-to-first-token, good for chat. but it can increase complexity with your front-end. we can show a sample streaming handler in both py/ts.
[03:20] Jordan: circling back to auth — Samira, walk through service account creation and KMS flow in the sandbox.
[03:27] Samira: sure. in the sandbox we'll create a service account tied to the customer's org id, then generate a short-lived SA token by calling our token exchange endpoint. the SA token is encrypted with your KMS CMK at rest. for rotation we can plug into your vault/GCP rotation.
[03:46] Alex: is the KMS handshake audited? we need audit logs for compliance.
[03:50] Samira: yes — audit logs are available in the private control plane and accessible via our console and streaming webhooks. we'll share our SOC2 excerpt and an example audit log format.
[04:05] Casey: and RBAC? can we limit which teams can call certain models?
[04:10] Samira: yep, RBAC is supported — per-team token scopes, per-model access controls in the console. we can map to your SSO groups via SAML.
[04:22] Priya: any gotchas with embedding storage? we plan to use embeddings for semantic search.
[04:27] Samira: embeddings storage is optional; you can use your own vector DB. we also support redwood-managed embeddings with configurable retention, but for regulated data we recommend self-hosted DB + encrypted-at-rest flows.
[04:45] Jordan: quick pause — Priya, are there any internal stakeholders beyond engineering who want to join the pilot? security / legal?
[04:53] Priya: yes, security will want to review the audit flows. legal will likely be involved once pricing is committed.
[05:01] Jordan: perfect — we'll include a security packet in the follow-up.
[05:08] Samira: jumping to sandbox provisioning — I'll walk through the repo. step 1: create org in console, step 2: create service account, step 3: bind KMS key, step 4: provision demo tokens. sample commands live in repo under /examples/onramp.
[05:30] Samira: note that CI example uses short-lived tokens minted by a CI job: you fetch a one-hour token, then immediately call the SDK. this prevents secrets in runners.
[05:44] Alex: what about local dev — can we use a persisted dev key?
[05:48] Samira: yes, dev keys are allowed for local testing but flagged in audit logs; don't use them in CI.
[05:56] Priya: can you show the console areas for cost and token-level breakdown?
[06:03] Samira: switching to console — here is the per-route cost breakdown, token-level billing, and latency percentile chart. you can set up alerts for latency regressions and token cost spikes.
[06:24] Jordan: optimize recommendations — Samira, can you outline batching and quantization suggestions for our chat load?
[06:30] Samira: for many short messages, small batching windows help (50-150ms) combined with prefix KV cache for repeated contexts. also consider a quantized model flavor for non-critical paths to reduce tokens per GPU. we'll run model profiling in the pilot.
[06:52] Alex: any differences when using Dedicated vs Hosted for batching behavior?
[06:56] Samira: Dedicated gives predictable concurrency and the autoscaler can be tuned; hosted is multi-tenant so very aggressive batching behavior might vary. fallback policies exist to route to cheaper/compatible variants under pressure.
[07:12] Jordan: cost question — can you ballpark unit cost differences?
[07:16] Samira: rough ballpark: hosted might be 10-20% cheaper for small scale due to shared capacity but Dedicated wins at scale because of reserved capacity and ability to use quantized instances. i'll send a worksheet.
[07:30] Priya: timeline — we want to be in pilot by 5/12. is that realistic?
[07:35] Jordan: yes if we get the sandbox and traffic profile this week.
[07:40] Casey: on the topic of logs — what gets logged in the audit vs request logs?
[07:44] Samira: request logs include metadata (request id, model, latency) but we never log raw customer prompts for private deployments; for hosted we offer options and redaction hooks.
[07:58] Alex: about the SDK examples — can you send a sample node/express middleware to handle streaming tokens and SSE?
[08:04] Samira: yes, we'll add an example.
[08:10] Jordan: ok let's do a short live demo of provisioning. Samira, demo create org flow.
[08:14] Samira: typing — creating org -> creating service account -> binding KMS key. sometimes the UI shows an error but it's a race in the example; ignore that in the demo.
[08:34] Priya: that UI looks clean. what's the model catalog policy? can we pin a specific model family?
[08:40] Samira: yep, you can pin versions and set rollout policies (canary, A/B). versions appear in the catalog and you can auto-fallback to smaller variants.
[08:52] Jordan: question from Priya on data residency: can we restrict data to our region?
[08:57] Samira: with Private or Dedicated in-region offering, yes. hosted has region options but not strict physical residency guarantees unless you contract for private deployment.
[09:10] Priya: good. we'll need that for EU customer data.
[09:14] Alex: what happens to KV cache when we switch models or versions?
[09:18] Samira: KV cache is model-variant specific; switching models invalidates incompatible cache. we maintain cache warmers during rollouts if you enable the option.
[09:33] Jordan: any blockers we haven't covered?
[09:36] Priya: mostly security docs and a proof of key rotation.
[09:40] Casey: plus a sample load script to validate latency at 99th percentile.
[09:44] Jordan: we'll deliver those.
[09:47] Samira: final notes on the SDK — there's a small gotcha: older SDK versions used env REDWOOD_API_KEY only, newer flows prefer REDWOOD_SA_TOKEN for short-lived tokens. we'll include a migration note.
[10:02] Alex: can you speak to observability integration — do you emit traces to our datadog?
[10:06] Samira: yes we export tracing headers and have a datadog exporter; we can show an example trace with token breakdown.
[10:18] Jordan: ok let's recap and lock next steps.
[10:22] Priya: sounds good. please include security contacts for our team.
[10:26] Jordan: noted. i'll add security contacts and send the pricing worksheet.
[10:30] Samira: i'll provision sandbox and post the repo link with examples.
[10:34] Alex: i'll collect and share traffic profile and SLOs.
[10:38] Casey: we're good, thanks.
[10:40] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up tomorrow with the pack.
[10:44] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription quality: some product names and acronyms mis-transcribed (e.g., K-V cash, redwood optimise vs optimize). occasional speaker overlaps and filler words preserved.
